Heights and diameters of Scots pine trees

Source: R/data.R
PineHeightDiameter.Rd

Heights and diameters at breast height (1.3 m above the ground) of 1678 Scots pine trees on 56 fixed-area sample plots in Ilomantsi, eastern Finland, collected by Timo Pukkala, for height-diameter models: the height grows with the diameter towards an asymptote, from the breast height of 1.3 m.

Usage

PineHeightDiameter

Format

A data frame with 1678 rows and 6 variables:

plot

identifier of the sample plot, a factor

dbh

diameter at breast height in cm

height

tree height in m

ntrees

number of trees on the plot

dmean

mean diameter of the trees on the plot, in cm

dvar

variance of the diameters of the trees on the plot

Source

The data set spati2 of the package lmfor (version 1.7, licence GPL-2), with the variables renamed. The script that converts it is in the directory data-raw of the source package.

References

Pukkala, T. (1989). Prediction of tree diameter and height in a Scots pine stand as a function of the spatial pattern of trees. Silva Fennica 23, 83-99. doi:10.14214/sf.a15532

Mehtätalo, L. and Lappi, J. (2020). Biometry for Forestry and Environmental Data: with Examples in R. Chapman and Hall/CRC, New York. doi:10.1201/9780429173462

Examples

# a Chapman-Richards curve from the breast height, the intercept b4 = 1.3, with a random asymptote
# of each plot
fit <- gcTMB(height ~ dbh, rform=b1 ~ 1 | plot, data=PineHeightDiameter,
             model="chapmanrichards", start=c(b4=1.3))
summary(fit)
